sources.ref: Walkplay Android app 2.3.1 (com.ttgk.musicbox): the KT register EQ screen (what an apply and a save send) and its filter type list

meta.notes: Walkplay's own app drives SchemeNo17 as a KT Micro register device, not with the Walkplay protocol: 5 bands from register 0x26, each band a gain register (s16 dB x 10, then the frequency) and a Q register (u16 x 1000, then the type), the same layout as Kiwi Ears and Tanchjim. Three things differ. The frequency register holds half the Hz, rounded down, and the app doubles what it reads back. The type byte is the type code plus 8 (bit 3 always set), and the app masks it with 7 on a read. The app writes register 0x24 with a 1 after the bands, where Kiwi Ears' firmware takes it first; that register is also the EQ switch there. Each write waits up to a second for the device's answer, and the app carries on whatever comes back. A save adds the commit. The bridge does the same, and also writes the DAC offset slider as the Global Gain control: register 0x3b, a step in a 16-entry table (0 mutes, 13 is 0 dB, 1.5 dB each), of which the slider reaches -6 to +3 dB, steps 9 to 15. The editor offers peaking, low shelf, high pass and low pass (no high shelf), 20 to 20000 Hz, gain +/-10 dB in 0.1 dB steps and Q 0.1 to 5 (typed as a decimal, 0.001 on the wire), with no pre-gain besides the DAC offset. These are the app's editor limits, and nothing here is confirmed on a device. The bridge does not write the register where the app records which of its own presets is selected (0x02); we have no meaningful index to put there, so the app may show a stale selection after a push. The app has no EQ off switch for these devices; the bridge can still write 0 to register 0x24, which is how Kiwi Ears' KT firmware turns its EQ off. Walkplay's product catalog lists the Kiwi Ears AD1 under this scheme, but Kiwi Ears' own app writes it in whole Hz; it has its own profile, which wins. devicePEQ differs: it drives this scheme with its Walkplay handler (5 bands, peaking and shelves, +/-10 dB). Out of scope: the app's microphone (ADC) EQ and ADC gain register 0x3a, and a flash erase command.
